newsitem.title: USA: Schult Homes CEO backs 1997 EPS view.
newsitem.headline: Schult Homes CEO backs 1997 EPS view.

text.p: Schult Homes Corp president and chief executive Walter Wells said Tuesday he is comfortable with the First Call estimate of $2.40 per share for fiscal 1997.
The company reported $1.81 per share for fiscal 1996.
The company is in the middle of its third quarter, for which First Call estimates $0.18 in earnings per share, down from the $0.22 reported for last year's period.

"The third quarter will probably be closer to flat, but we just can't tell," said company vice president of finance Fred Greenawalt, in an interview with Reuters. "The question on that is whatever March will bring."
The company, which produces manufactured and modular homes, said last month it expected its performance in the third quarter to be relatively flat compared with a year ago.
So far this winter has handed the company more snow-related lost shipment days than it has had in three years, Wells said.
"The weather has impacted us significantly," Wells said. "In Minnesota we've had blizzard after blizzard. Shipments have been restricted. And in the Northwest, we've had unusually severe weather."
In the Midwest and the East, Wells said the company has had a normal winter business pattern.
"It's been more severe in Minnesota and Oregon, but in the rest of the country its been pretty normal," Wells said.
Wells said he sees "a significant opportunity to achieve a (annual) 10 percent growth rate and to significantly improve on earnings before interest and taxes."
The roughly 20 percent increases in manufactured housing enjoyed by the industry during the early 1990s surely won't continue, Wells said.
"Now the work is cutting out a significant portion of the competitors' market," he said.
Wells said the company plans to increase its mid-to-low range market niche by adding capacity to three existing plants by the end of fiscal 1999.
The plants will produce the company's traditional high-end homes and a new line of lower-to-mid-priced homes. The plants will share overhead including inventory, service departments and sales forces.

The company's first two dual-line plants, in Navasota, Texas and Herminston, Ore., have been successful, Wells said. Another is planned for Buckeye, Ariz., and two more locations will be announced in the near future, Wells said.
The three additional dual line plants will make it possible for the company to increase its capacity from its current level of just over $400 million to about $500 million per year, Wells said.
"These five locations will produce two-thirds of our product when they are fully functional, by the end of fiscal 2000," Greenawalt said.
"We have commitments from our dealers to fill this capacity," Wells said.
Wells said the company's expansion will be funded by its $10 million credit line. Wells said the company is essentially debt free.
Greenawalt predicted the company will sell between 17,000 to 17,500 sections during fiscal 1997. During fiscal 1996 the company sold about 15,500 sections.
